summary: Slide a threshold and watch precision, recall and the ROC curve trade places.
headline: One model, many possible scores
overview: A classifier gives each case a score. Where you draw the threshold decides who gets flagged. Raise it and you flag fewer, with more of them right. Lower it and you catch more, with more false alarms.
Precision asks how many flags were right. Recall asks how many real cases were found. The ROC curve shows every threshold at once, and AUC squeezes it into one number.

break.label: Break it
break.explains: Flag everything. Recall hits 100%, and precision collapses to the share of cases that were positive anyway.

check.question: You lower the threshold. What usually happens?
options: Recall rises, precision tends to fall

realLife: A medical screening test favours recall, since a missed case is costly. A spam filter that deletes real mail favours precision.
data: Four hundred cases, half truly yes. Scores come from two overlapping bell curves, one centred at 0.40 for no and one at 0.62 for yes. The seed is fixed.
maths: AUC is the chance a random positive scores higher than a random negative.
code:
from sklearn.metrics import precision_score, recall_score, roc_auc_score
precision_score(y, s >= 0.5), recall_score(y, s >= 0.5), roc_auc_score(y, s)
